Penguin’s opened La otra aventura y otros escritos page (S129, lines 408–416) places Unos días en el Brasil among five distinct nonfiction originals and calls it a diary of a 1960 PEN Club trip, while Barral’s 2014 proceedings article (S136, printed p.137 / PDF p.1, lines 31–36) explicitly labels it a posthumous 2010 travel diary. The 1991, posthumous 2010, and current publisher-product records therefore establish a real edition/selection identity boundary; keep the whole object deferred until those editions can be reconciled. CVC Bibliografía L6 lists “El génesis de los guaraníes. Leyenda de la creación y destrucción del mundo” in Revista del Ateneo Paraguayo (1948). Enrique Flores, “Las ‘culturas condenadas’: el mitólogo como compilador,” Revista Telar 27 (2021), directly states that the 1948 text was taken/translated from Nimuendajú’s original (Dialnet article PDF physical p.2 L55–79), and its note 18 calls the 1971 El génesis de los Apapokuva-guaraní a “reedición” (PDF physical p.10 L283–284). The same five song titles listed for the 1948 text at PDF p.2 L78–79 correspond to the five poems in the near-contemporary 1971 Alcor issue review (S217, Caravelle 18, pp.173–196; title at p.22 and poem listings from p.25; also S219/CVC chronology L25 spells Apapokura). These records establish a 1971 bibliographic item but conflict with treating it as a distinct first-publication-year 1971 work. No physical 1971 Alcor/book artifact or full contents/title-page collation has been obtained. Therefore work identity, 1948-versus-1971 first-publication year, title/spelling relation (Apapokuva/Apapokura), and exact re-edition scope remain unresolved; W211 is deferred, not admitted as an independent 1971 work.
